summary: npm package ships Linux binary implementing a WebRTC-driven remote shell agent
details: The package tarball contains a 13 MB Linux/amd64 Go binary at bin/sxt that implements a remote-terminal agent: it embeds a PTY spawner (creack/pty), os/exec with /bin/sh and /bin/bash, a full pion WebRTC stack (DataChannel, SCTP, DTLS, ICE/STUN/TURN), and a coder/websocket signaling client. Compiled strings include a `/signaling` endpoint on a `.sextant.`-branded host and `authorization` header handling. The dataflow is network-in to PTY-out: a remote peer negotiates a WebRTC session through the signaling server and drives an interactive shell on the host running the binary, yielding full-host remote code execution. Publisher metadata reinforces the mismatch: package.json's license field points to https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control, and the same module path github.com/ddos798/claude_control is compiled into bin/sxt — a `ddos`-prefixed, `claude_control`-named source repository inconsistent with the advertised `sextant-cli` branding.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
